item.title: Could freezing coral larvae protect reefs from ocean warming?
item.description: As coral reefs worldwide face warming seas and ocean acidification, scientists in the Pacific turn to ‘cryopreservation’.

item.title: Rise in mild Karachi earthquakes prompts calls for disaster preparedness
item.description: The city’s building codes need enforcing, and the groundwater extraction that destabilises buildings needs controlling, say experts.

item.title: Asia-Pacific faces ‘US$500 billion a year’ hit from rising seas if current policies continue
item.description: Coastal flooding could bring US$500 billion of annual damages to the Asia-Pacific by the year 2100, if countries do not adapt to rising sea levels.

item.title: Philippines under pressure to improve the rights of nickel miners amid global talks on critical minerals
item.description: Will the inclusion of language on labour rights at the world’s biggest climate talks be the fundamental step to ease their plight?

item.title: The critical minerals race is putting the planet at risk
item.description: Robust legal frameworks, backed by effective enforcement, can create the conditions for stable and rights-respecting mining. That means safeguarding Indigenous rights, protecting water resources and well-governed impact assessments.

item.title: Japan revamps aviation-based CO2 monitoring to preserve decades-old climate datasets
item.description: The move ensures the continuity of one of the world’s longest-running aviation climate datasets as older jets are retired.

item.title: Malaysian regulators to act on companies not complying with sustainability reporting requirements
item.description: Financial authorities in Malaysia said they would adopt a “phased and practical” approach to address non-compliance of the National Sustainability Reporting Framework by corporations.

item.title: Asia’s AI real estate boom reaches Singapore, bringing efficiency and new risks
item.description: AI is reshaping how buildings are run, from cooling systems to construction planning. Yet experts warn that the technology’s heavy electricity demand could undermine sustainability gains.

item.title: After COP30, Brazilian oil continues its rush towards the global market
item.description: A decision to drill at the mouth of the Amazon drew criticism at the UN summit. But Brazil’s oil production still soars, as it hopes to consolidate its role as an exporter.

item.title: Global leaders press for environmental action even as divisions widen
item.description: The United Nations Environment Assembly takes place this week in Nairobi, at a time when wars, protectionist economic policies and global divisions are undermining nations’ ability to reach consensus on climate change, biodiversity loss and pollution – issues that require collective action.
